Synopsis:
Major US banks (JPMorgan, BofA, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, Citigroup) delivered blockbuster Q2 2026 earnings, driven by record trading revenues, surging investment banking fees (SpaceX IPO ~$500M in fees, Cerebras $6.4B IPO, Alphabet $85B share sale), and a dealmaking boom not seen since 2021. Global IB revenue hit $61.4B in H1 2026, up 24% YoY. Despite the euphoria, multiple CEOs and CFOs explicitly flagged forward risks: elevated leverage and valuations (JPMorgan), sticky inflation and tight monetary policy (BofA), geopolitical tensions and fiscal deficits (Dimon), and unsustainably strong conditions (Wells Fargo).
